statement: Let V be a vector space over a field K of scalars, and let T: V -> V be a linear transformation. A nonzero vector v in V is an eigenvector of T corresponding to eigenvalue lambda in K if and only if T(v) = lambda * v. In matrix form for an n x n square matrix A, an eigenvector is a nonzero vector v satisfying A * v = lambda * v, or equivalently (A - lambda * I) * v = 0.

symbols.meaning: linear transformation mapping vector space V to itself
matrix representation of a linear transformation

symbols.dimensions: n x n (or operator on V)

symbols.meaning: vector space over scalar field K
eigenspace (characteristic space) associated with lambda, equal to {v : T(v) = lambda * v}

properties.property: Any nonzero scalar multiple of an eigenvector is also an eigenvector corresponding to the same eigenvalue.
properties.why: Linearity of T gives T(alpha * v) = alpha * T(v) = alpha * lambda * v = lambda * (alpha * v)

properties.property: The set of all eigenvectors associated with an eigenvalue lambda together with the zero vector forms the eigenspace E = {v : T(v) = lambda * v}, which is the kernel of the linear transformation T - lambda * I.
properties.why: T(v) = lambda * v is equivalent to (T - lambda * I)v = 0

properties.property: For an n x n matrix A, eigenvectors associated with lambda are nontrivial solutions to (A - lambda * I)v = 0, which exist if and only if det(A - lambda * I) = 0.
properties.why: Nontrivial solutions to the homogeneous linear system require the matrix (A - lambda * I) to be singular

properties.property: For differential operators acting on infinite-dimensional function spaces, functions satisfying D f(t) = lambda * f(t) are eigenvectors commonly called eigenfunctions.
properties.why: Differential operators are linear transformations acting on function spaces

assumptions.assumption: The vector v must be nonzero (v != 0).
assumptions.breaks_when: v = 0, which satisfies T(0) = lambda * 0 trivially for every scalar lambda and is explicitly excluded by definition.

assumptions.assumption: The transformation T maps a vector space into itself (T: V -> V, or matrix A is square n x n).
assumptions.breaks_when: T maps between different spaces V -> W where V != W (or A is rectangular m x n with m != n), making T(v) and lambda * v elements of different spaces that cannot be equated.

assumptions.assumption: The scalar lambda belongs to the base field K of the vector space V.
assumptions.breaks_when: The roots of the characteristic polynomial lie outside the scalar field K (e.g., complex eigenvalues for a vector space defined strictly over the real field R).

failure_modes.mode: Zero vector chosen as an eigenvector
failure_modes.signature: v = 0 is identified as an eigenvector
failure_modes.cause: Violating the defining condition that an eigenvector must be a nonzero vector.

failure_modes.mode: No nonzero solutions to (A - lambda * I)v = 0
failure_modes.signature: (A - lambda * I)v = 0 yields only the trivial solution v = 0
failure_modes.cause: The parameter lambda is not a root of det(A - lambda * I) = 0, meaning (A - lambda * I) is invertible with a trivial kernel.

failure_modes.mode: Absence of real eigenvectors due to complex eigenvalues
failure_modes.signature: No vectors with real entries satisfy A * v = lambda * v
failure_modes.cause: The matrix has complex conjugate eigenvalues whose corresponding eigenvectors have imaginary components, which do not exist in R^n.
